TITLE — typeset this exact headline, large, high-contrast, in the vertical middle 60% of the frame. No other words, no byline, no watermark, no logo:
Your 80% coverage badge is lying: gate on branches, not just lines

SUBJECT
Wire a c8 coverage gate that fails the build on untested code — and why 100% line coverage can still hide a whole branch that never ran once.

NOTES
There is a special kind of confidence that comes from a 100% coverage badge sitting at the top of your README, glowing like a productivity halo. It says: every line of this code has been run by a test. It does not say — and this is the whole problem — that every line was run for the right reasons . Line coverage counts the lines your tests touched. It does not count the decisions your code makes on those lines. A , an , a — one line, two futures, and your test suite only ever visited one of them

Draw the concrete apparatus this article is about — not a generic circuit board, robot, brain, or rocket. No faces. No UI chrome. No stock-tech collage. The still frame must read at 300px.
